reason: S1 adds a configurable LZMA decoding mode through QUIRK_ALLOW_NON_ZERO_INITIAL_BYTE and makes the Lzip decoder enable it automatically. This creates a newly accepted input class where the LZMA initial byte is non-zero. H0 exclusively initializes and drives wuffs_json__decoder and wuffs_aux::DecodeJson, so no input, hash-derived configuration, or execution path in H0 can reach either the new LZMA quirk protocol or the Lzip integration. Although lack of LZMA/Lzip coverage existed in S0, the newly introduced permissive branch and automatic Lzip configuration are S1-specific behavior, materially aggravating the gap.
evidence: lzma.decoder gains the state field allow_non_zero_initial_byte.
QUIRK_ALLOW_NON_ZERO_INITIAL_BYTE is newly declared as 0x5058_E000 | 0x00, while QUIRK_FORMAT_EXTENSION moves to 0x5058_E000 | 0x01.
lzma.decoder.set_quirk! now controls allow_non_zero_initial_byte, and lzma.decoder.get_quirk exposes its state.
lzma.decoder.do_transform_io? changes the rejection condition from c8 <> 0x00 to (c8 <> 0x00) and not this.allow_non_zero_initial_byte.
lzip.decoder.do_transform_io? now calls this.lzma.set_quirk!(key: lzma.QUIRK_ALLOW_NON_ZERO_INITIAL_BYTE, value: 1) before decoding.
H0's fuzz_complex and fuzz_simple only call wuffs_json__decoder__initialize and wuffs_json__decoder__decode_tokens; fuzz_cpp only calls wuffs_aux::DecodeJson.
H0's g_quirks contains only WUFFS_JSON__QUIRK_* identifiers and cannot select either LZMA quirk.
recommended_action: Add a LZMA/Lzip fuzz entry point, or extend an appropriate codec harness, so fuzz-controlled inputs exercise both zero and non-zero initial bytes and fuzz-controlled configuration toggles QUIRK_ALLOW_NON_ZERO_INITIAL_BYTE; also cover the Lzip path that enables the quirk automatically.
